claims.claim: Augustine of Hippo was bishop of Hippo from 396 to 430.
The sermon was preached in the presence of Emeritus, a Donatist bishop.
Augustine visited Caesarea in 418 on the orders of Pope Zosimus to settle some ecclesiastical necessity that had arisen there.
During his visit to Caesarea, Augustine encountered the Donatist Bishop Emeritus and unsuccessfully attempted to persuade him to return to Catholic unity.
The meeting between Augustine and Emeritus seems to have been fortuitous rather than the pretext for the visit.
While at Caesarea, Augustine also prevailed on the citizens to discontinue the Caterva, an organized local brawl.
The sermon states that outside the Catholic Church one can have everything except salvation, including honor, sacraments, alleluia, Amen, the Gospel, faith, and preaching.
The work survives in Migne's Patrologia Latina, volume 43, columns 689-698.
Augustine mentions the sermon in his Retractations, Book II, chapter 77.
